newsitem.title: AFRICA: Ex-warlord Taylor declared Liberia's new president.
newsitem.headline: Ex-warlord Taylor declared Liberia's new president.

text.p: Former warlord Charles Taylor won election as Liberia's new president on Thursday with a landslide victory in weekend polling to end seven years of civil war.
The head of the West African nation's election commission said that Taylor, who launched the war in 1989, took 75.3 percent of the vote in Saturday's elections.

Former senior U.N. official Ellen Johnson-Sirleaf was runner up with just under 9.6 percent, commission chairman Henry Andrews told a packed hall at commission headquarters in the Sinkor District of the capital Monrovia.
Thousands of Liberians thronged the streets outside.

Twelve candidates took part. The turnout was approaching 90 percent. Andrews said that results of polling for a 26-member Senate and a 64-seat House of Representatives would be announced in a few days.

The elections were the climax of a peace deal brokered by Liberia's West African neighbours to end the war which has killed well over 150,000 people. Freed American slaves founded Liberia as Africa's first independent republic in 1847.
Taylor, dressed in a trade-mark cream safari suit, smiled broadly as Andrews announced his tally at the end of the list of results. He made no formal comment.
Defeated candidates crossed over to congratulate Taylor but neither Johnson-Sirleaf nor Taylor's fellow former warlord Alhaji Kromah attended the ceremony.
The third former warlord in the field, George Boley, was present at the ceremony.
